newsitem.title: USA: Dade Cty, Fla., eyes commercial paper for airport.
newsitem.headline: Dade Cty, Fla., eyes commercial paper for airport.

text.p: Florida's Dade County is seeking authorization to issue up to $400 million of commercial paper to manage cash flow between bond issues for the $3.2 billion Miami airport expansion.

The authorization request went before the Dade County Commission's finance committee Friday but the committee could not vote for lack of a quorum. The proposal was forwarded to the full commission without recommendation.
The county has not issued commercial paper since the last major airport expansion in the 1980s. The magnitude of the current project makes it a good candidate.
"They don't want to issue bonds for that kind of money up front," Dade Finance Director Rachel Baum said.

If the county can get the commercial paper program approved and the RFPs done before the commission recesses in August, it could delay a $200 million airport revenue bond issue that otherwise must be done by Oct. 1 to continue funding construction.

The county plans to continue financing the expansion with revenue bond issues in the $200 million to $300 million range about every six months to a year. It would issue about $50 million of commercial paper at a time, issuing bonds and paying off the notes when the amount of paper oustanding reaches about three-quarters of the bond issue size.
"It gives us flexibility. We'll only issue the debt as we need it," Commissioner Jimmy Morales, who heads the finance commitee, said.
The short-term borrowing would reduce debt costs and would not have to be reflected immediately in the airport rate schedules, said the county's bond administrator, Lidia Monzon-Aguirre.
Airports in Orlando, Tampa, San Francisco and Atlanta, among others have used similar debt issues for construction programs, she said.

Morales said the issue should be opened to banks and other underwriters outside the county's standing pool of underwriters, even if that means reducing minority participation. Many underwriters in the pool do not do commercial paper, he said.
"If there are players out there who are players in that field, we would be short-changing ourselves if we didn't open it up," Morales said.

The finance committee also forwarded to the full commission an authorization request for $100 million of bond anticipation notes for its water-sewer department. The authorization would be continuing so that it could issue additional notes as the outstanding ones are repaid, as long as it does not have more than $100 million outstanding at a time.
